title: Coarse run then downscale: do a kerb, a crown and a small hollow survive?
process: a coarse run mapped onto the 1 m ground against the known answer on the 1 m ground: whether street detail survives, how much faster, how much worse
executor: node (CPU surface solver) and browser (GPU); raw measurements in street/raw/, scored by run.mjs
equations: at rest the pond stands at the level the rain volume fills on the 1 m ground, whatever grid ran
the 1 m map of a coarse run: the water surface carried onto the 1 m ground (src/downscale.js), or the subgrid tables' level (src/subgrid.js)

kerb and crown: rain on one side of a crowned street behind kerbs ponds in that side's gutter at the level its volume fills; while that level is below the kerb and the crown, the lot behind the kerb and the far gutter hold nothing
hollow: a 3 x 3 m hollow at the low point of a yard holds the rain of the 176 m^2 that drain to it: depth = P x 176 / 9
boundaryConditions: surface closed on all sides; no drainage Detail scenes: the kerbed street is closed on all sides; the hollow lot is closed except its foot, a free-outfall edge.
geometry: the bowl neighbourhood, 100-yr storm, no drainage (PV-SS8 case none-100 is the 1 m run). Detail scenes (terrain.mjs): kerbStreet, a 24 x 16 m street with a 0.08 m crown, 0.15 m kerbs on odd metres and rain on the south side only; hollowLot, a 16 x 16 m lot at 2 % with a 3 x 3 m hollow 0.15 m deep at x, y 5-8 m. hollowYard (the scene the hollow cases use after the second definition revision): the same lot with the ground above the hollow falling to it from both sides and a berm below it, so that exactly 176 m^2 drain to the hollow

cases.unit: grid: F m cells with downscaling, or the subgrid mode

solver: FloodSim surface solver with the app's settings (hdry 1e-5 m, hfront 1e-3 m, dtDry 2 s; MUSCL minmod, HLLC, SSP-RK2, CFL 0.48). cpu rows: src/solver-cpu.js (fp64). gpu rows: src/solver-gpu.js in Chrome WebGPU (fp32). 2 m, 4 m: coarsen and downscale. 4s, 8s: the subgrid speed and screening modes (GPU only).

reference.independence: the end level is arithmetic; the peak has no hand answer, so the 1 m run stands in and those rows are Not independently validated

outputs: end pond level on the 1 m map against the arithmetic level
peak wall depth at each house against the 1 m run (root mean square over the houses)
houses exposed (10 cm rule) against the 1 m run
reported: wall time against the 1 m run on the same executor
detail scenes, on the 1 m map at the end: the depth in the gutter the rain fell beside; the depth on the lot behind the kerb; the depth in the far gutter; the depth in the hollow
criteriaNotes: End level: 1 cm. Against the 1 m run: 5 cm root mean square on the wall depths and nine houses in ten given the same exposed / not exposed answer; these rows carry the status Not independently validated because the reference is the same solver. Revision 2, the pass rule in Kyle's terms: after a coarse run is mapped to 1 m, a KERB survives if the lot behind it holds under 1 cm and the gutter holds its depth within 2 cm; a CROWN survives if the far gutter holds under 1 cm; a HOLLOW survives if its depth is within 2 cm of the hand answer. 1 m stays the baseline and is held to the same rule.
resolution: 1 m; 2 m and 4 m with downscaling; 4 m and 8 m subgrid
assumptions: the 1 m run is the best available answer for the peak
limitations: one scene, one storm, no drainage
CPU wall times say little about the GPU: the speed-up that matters is the gpu rows'
the detail scenes are level along the street: a kerb and a crown are tested holding still water, not steering a flow
one kerb height, one crown height, one hollow size; each sits across 2 m and 4 m cell boundaries
validRange: ponding in a bowl; not sheet flow on a hillside
scoring: automated: street/score.mjs builds rows with lib/score.mjs row(); one row set per executor (cpu, gpu), never merged; a case with no raw file is listed as not run and has no rows

criteriaRevisions.why: first registration, before any sandbox case was run

two criteria added for the detail cases (detailDepthAbsM, detailDryM); the three registered in revision 1 are unchanged. Reason: Kyle's direction of 17 Nov 2026 that coarse-then-downscale is a pass or fail question about kerbs, crowns and small hollows.

definitionRevisions.why: revision 2, after the first CPU run of the bowl cases: Kyle's direction (relayed by the product session) that 1 m stays the baseline and that this case must say whether a kerb, a street crown and a small hollow survive a coarse run. Ten detail cases, two scenes and two criteria were added; the bowl cases, their criteria and their results are unchanged. The detail cases were registered before any of them ran.

after the first CPU run of the three plain hollow cases, which all read 0.18 m against a hand answer of 0.11 m, the 1 m baseline included: a setup error of mine, not a model result. The lot was closed at its foot, so the lot's runoff ponded 0.14 m deep against the foot wall and drowned the hollow; the hand answer is for a hollow standing alone. The foot of the lot is now the free-outfall edge. Criteria unchanged (same hash). The hollow cases were run again; the first raw files are kept and their rows stand in results/2026-11-17T19-13-18-241Z as an invalid setup.

second change to the hollow cases, after their second CPU run. With the foot open, the 1 m run filled the hollow to its rim (0.150 m) where the hand answer was 0.110 m, 2 m read 0.120 m and 4 m 0.100 m. The hand answer took the hollow's catchment to be the strip directly upslope of it (33 m^2); on the grid the cells beside the hollow also shed part of their sheet flow sideways into it. Neither is exact, so the case had no unambiguous answer: an invalid setup, not a model failure and not a pass for the coarse grids. The hollow now sits at the low point of a yard closed by a berm (scene hollowYard), where everything above it must enter it, and the storm is 5 mm so the hollow does not fill. Criteria unchanged (same hash). The first two sets of raw files are kept. The sideways capture is recorded in FINDINGS as an observation.
